takeaways: Senior living M&A is on pace for a record 2026 even with the 10-year up from about 4% to 5%+, as new institutional funds chase stabilized Class A and lenders trim spreads 20-30 bps; cap rates may drift up in 2027.
Tress and Robin were cleared to buy about 170 Genesis Healthcare skilled nursing facilities for roughly $1B out of bankruptcy, paying Welltower and Omega's $233M term loan in cash.

Fed Chair Warsh's remarks reinforce an October pause after September's hike, while real estate fundraising fell 31% through September with residential and industrial taking over three-quarters of sector-specific capital.

items.headline: Senior living M&A sprints toward record 2026 despite rate volatility
items.summary: Ikaria's Jason Dopoulos says 2026 is nearly matching 2025's record transaction count through October, with new funds from Clarion, AEW, Artemis and Silver Wave chasing stabilized Class A. The 10-year rose from about 4% in February to about 5.1%; lenders cut spreads 20-30 bps, and cap rates compressed 25-50 bps through September but could rise modestly in 2027.

items.headline: Tress and Robin cleared to buy Genesis Healthcare SNFs for about $1B
items.summary: 101 West, the NewGen affiliate of Abe Tress and Aaron Robin, got final approval to buy about 170 Genesis skilled nursing facilities out of bankruptcy for roughly $1B. The plan pays Welltower and Omega's $233M term loan in cash, sets a $150M settlement and leaves existing equity with no recovery. (via The Promote)

items.headline: Warsh remarks reinforce expectations for an October rate pause
items.summary: Fed Chair Warsh says the economy has largely tracked policymakers' expectations since the September rate increase, reinforcing expectations the Fed holds in October and keeping rate-path uncertainty central for CRE financing.

items.headline: Real estate fundraising drops 31% as residential and industrial capture capital
items.summary: Real estate fundraising fell 31% through September, with residential and industrial taking more than three-quarters of sector-specific capital raised, a tougher raise environment for other strategies.

items.headline: SlateView launches with $500M target, buys two California communities
items.summary: The new firm, founded by ex-NorthStar Healthcare CEO Kendall Young and Azhar Jameeli, bought Parkview Estates (Fountain Valley) and Meadowbrook at Agoura Hills, operated by Discovery and Integral. It plans $8-10M of renovations and targets 120+ unit communities in high-barrier West and East Coast markets.

items.headline: EQT buys Stockbridge in $375M deal
items.summary: EQT is acquiring Stockbridge for $375M plus an option for $175M of performance bonuses. Stockbridge claims $27.5B AUM, but the deal emphasizes $16.5B of fee-generating assets, and it will fold into EQT Real Estate. (via The Promote)

items.headline: Pontegadea pays $550M for Chicago's One North Wacker
items.summary: Amancio Ortega's family office bought the 94%-leased tower from Donald Bren at about $390/sf, the largest Chicago office deal in a decade and one of the year's biggest U.S. office trades. (via The Promote)

items.headline: Six AI investment opportunities beyond data centers
items.summary: ULI and Heitman point to emerging uses for existing buildings plus nearer-term demand for power, batteries and construction-support properties.

items.headline: Melinda French Gates' 48-hour rule for criticizing employees
items.summary: She gives feedback within 48 hours of being unhappy with work, so she can cool off and be clear, and says silence after 48 hours means the work was good. 'Being clear is kind.'

items.headline: Cain pitches One Beverly Hills buyers on 'Founder Bonds'
items.summary: Cain International is offering 5% Founder Bonds, typically about 30% of sales price, to condo buyers to fund construction around California's deposit ban. They sit junior to a $2.8B JPMorgan-led senior loan and $1.5B Vici mezz; Cain has raised $350M and hopes for $1.3B more. (via The Promote)

items.headline: S2 completes $1.2B of loan mods; Rise48 nears $600M+ Nomura refi
items.summary: Scott Everett's S2 finished mods and refis on an 8K+ unit portfolio and settled with Capital One over $11.5M of guarantees. Rise48 is nearing a $600M+ Nomura refi on about 4,800 units, with about $550M to be securitized on two-year debt. (via The Promote)

items.headline: Apartment insurance costs outpace revenue across 30 states
items.summary: GlobeSt reports apartment insurance costs are growing faster than revenue in 30 states, a margin pressure that also applies to senior housing operators.

items.headline: Multifamily delinquency: private-label CMBS holds half
items.summary: Private-label CMBS accounts for about half of multifamily delinquency, per CRE Daily.

items.headline: Fifth Wall sees AI broadening proptech investment beyond real estate software
items.summary: Fifth Wall says AI is widening proptech investment opportunities beyond traditional real estate software, alongside continued funding momentum for construction and CRE startups.

items.headline: Costco CEO Ron Vachris: 'Don't chase a title'
items.summary: Vachris rose from forklift driver to CEO without a college degree and credits staying focused over title-chasing or job-hopping.

items.headline: Move slow and make things: Japanese craftsmanship in the age of AI
items.summary: Authors Matt Alt and David Schonthal argue craft lessons in quality and patience matter more as AI makes speed cheap.

items.headline: Gen Z started building wealth at 19, yet most feel they can't get ahead
items.summary: A U.S. Bank survey finds young adults start accumulating wealth about 13 years earlier than boomers did, but most still feel behind.

items.headline: Million-dollar-income renter households more than triple
items.summary: The number of renter households earning $1M or more has more than tripled, per GlobeSt, a sign of growing high-end rental demand.
